parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no documented universal-exposure measure (no bathroom/facility ban, no custody or border rule reaching visitors), and no organised targeting or state threat-framing. Positives are real: gender identity covered in goods-and-services anti-discrimination law since 2015, hate-crime sentencing enhancement, same-sex conduct lawful, an active NGO providing trans-inclusive legal aid and hormone/PrEP health access in cooperation with the ministry, and the state prosecuting an official who called for violence against LGBTQ people. Negatives are social hostility and uneven implementation: NGO reports of intolerance and hatred, common political hate speech, threats around Pride, and very low reporting to police. Trans-specific violence is undocumented (the 2015 LGBTQ-wide figures are dated and off-population), and border, custody and visitor-care practice are open questions, not documented exposures. Sits in the reduced-risk band, below acceptance-plus-working-protection jurisdictions.
